sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (territory of the Grand Duchy; no separate sub-state corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law (Napoleonic codified tradition, with Anglo-American-inspired financial services and fund legislation, including the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 21 November 2005, in force 1 December 2009)

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 12 March 1994, in force 28 June 1995)
Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 3 April 1996, in force 20 December 2000)
Multilateral Instrument (MLI) BEPS Convention (ratified 7 June 2019, in force 1 October 2019) modifying numerous Luxembourg DTAs
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated 2020, pending ratification and entry into force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended through the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2019 operating the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, and CSSF Circular 18/698 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; Law of 19 December 2020 on freezing and confiscation of assets; Luxembourg International Financial Sanctions regime administered by the Cellule de Suivi des Sanctions Financières Internationales (Ministry of Finance).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (each natural-person UBO and authorized signatory)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing national authority of the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961, in force for Luxembourg since 3 June 1970) for non-EU-issued passports; notarial certification for EU-issued passports

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility invoice or bank statement, issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or licensed credit institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille when issued outside the EU; otherwise notarized certified copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate partner and each corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for registries in contracting states; Consular Legalization via the Luxembourg consulate for non-contracting states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled Power of Attorney for the notarial deed signer (if the signer is not the statutory manager or a named partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent legalization authority of the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, failing this, Consular Legalization at the Embassy of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds declaration (with supporting accounting evidence for the capital contribution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Declarant UBO supported by bank statements issued by the transferring financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature certification; foreign documents authenticated via Hague Apostille where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Article 3 and Article 4 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02/Circular 18/698 for all natural-person UBOs and beneficial owners holding at least 25%; each UBO must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the Luxembourg national freezing decisions published by the Ministry of Finance; PEP status includes domestic, foreign and international organization PEPs plus family members and known close associates; screening is required at onboarding, before any distribution or reimbursement of capital, and continuously on a risk-triggered basis, with mandatory SAR reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) within 24 hours of a match confirmation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) front office, accessible at www.lbr.lu; name reservations are transmitted electronically by the drafting Luxembourg notary before execution of the SCSp deed
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be expressed in Latin characters; names in non-Latin scripts require a French, German or English transliteration to be filed in the RCS. The name must be lawful, distinctive, non-misleading and must not create confusion with existing registered entities or protected designations. For a Société en Commandite Spéciale, the name must incorporate the statutory suffix 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'; use of the French, English or Latin name variants is permitted. The name of a limited partner may not appear in the corporate name in a manner implying unlimited liability.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (reserved for credit institutions authorized by the CSSF)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance / Reinsurance (reserved for undertakings authorized by the Commissariat aux Assurances)
Fonds d'investissement / Fund / OPCVM / SICAV / SICAF / FCP / AIF (reserved for regulated collective investment vehicles)
SICAR / ARP / SE / SA / S.à r.l. (statutory form tokens misrepresenting the SCSp legal form)
Société de gestion / Management Company (reserved for CSSF-licensed fund or portfolio managers)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Settlement (reserved for financial market infrastructures)
Luxembourg / Grand-Duché de Luxembourg / État / municipal / administration publique (tokens implying a public-law body or official state connection, requiring prior Ministry of Justice approval)
Avocat / Notaire / Réviseur d'entreprises / Auditeur (regulated liberal professions requiring title protection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS name reservation is valid for one month from the date of notarial submission and cannot be extended as of right; a fresh reservation may be re-filed immediately after expiry. Upon rejection, the Luxembourg notary receives a written refusal memorandum, after which the promoters may (i) submit an amended or modified name on an urgent basis via the same notarial channel, preserving the existing filing timeline, or (ii) file a formal administrative appeal addressed to the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of the refusal; a subsequent judicial appeal is available before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 3 months. In parallel, the RCS accepts a request for priority re-examination of the refused name if the promoter submits a contextual explanation of distinctiveness and lawful use.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-regulated commercial SCSp, provided that the registered office is located in Luxembourg, that a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent or professional of the financial sector provides the registered office, and that the partnership maintains genuine administrative substance proportionate to its activity, including available management oversight, accounting records, banking relations and decision-making records; a purely passive letterbox model is administratively tolerated only for third-party-managed vehicles and substantially increases the risk of tax residency re-characterization, CFC attribution, denial of tax treaty access and municipal business tax assessment at the SCSp level.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15_percent_annual_probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the CSSF or the RCS at the domiciliation agent's premises for a Medium_Risk financial vehicle; 5_percent_direct_inspection_probability at the SCSp's registered office in the first 12 months post-incorporation, rising to 20_percent if the vehicle is classified as an unregulated alternative investment fund or if late filings or suspicious transaction reports occur.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and RCS availability verification through notarial channel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff; no RCS fee for the preliminary name reservation request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarial execution of the SCSp limited partnership agreement (LPA) and partnership deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; EUR 1,500 - EUR 2,500 per deed, excluding applicable VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and electronic filing fee (immatriculation de la société en commandite spéciale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff for electronic availability requests and corporate registration extracts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the SCSp formation deed and RCS data in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff levied per filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory zero-filing fee for B2C self-filing; agent processing costs quoted separately

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC package, PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening for all UBOs and general partner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate service provider / compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and multi-list continuous screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg legal opinion confirming SCSp valid constitution, tax pass-through eligibility and absence of financial-sector licensing requirement for royalty/revenue-based financing activity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (member of the Luxembourg Bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a structured legal opinion, EUR 4,000 - EUR 6,000 flat fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations and apostille/consular legalization of foreign corporate documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator, apostille authority of the issuing state, and competent Luxembourg consulate where required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per document; Luxembourg Ministry of Justice apostille counter fees where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional banking due diligence and account pre-approval support with a Luxembourg or EU credit institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate service provider / bank introduction desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; bank own account-opening fees billed separately by the credit institution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (including the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale), Articles 101-103 governing limited partnerships and the special limited partnership regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive partnership agreement (contrat de société / acte constitutif) executed by notarial deed or private writing, filed as an RCS registration submission (dépôt au RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account requirement; partnership capital (apports) is freely determined in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constituent meeting of the partners of the SCSp held in Luxembourg, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: (1) The partnership agreement is approved; the initial capital subscriptions of the General Partner and the Special Limited Partners are accepted, and the General Partner is directed to issue the capital interest confirmations. (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. (3) [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) with authority to open bank accounts, execute revenue-based financing agreements, collect royalties, engage counsel, and lodge filings with the RCS, tax authorities, and the beneficial ownership register. (4) All further formation formalities are ratified and delegated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the constitutive partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (for notarial form) or the partners by private deed; no government approval required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement identifying the General Partner (gérant), the Special Limited Partners, capital subscriptions, profit and royalty-sharing waterfall, and registered office. Execute by notarial deed or private writing; notarization is mandatory if real property is contributed. Verify that the General Partner possesses legal capacity and has no personal bankruptcy history.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the General Partner and all Special Limited Partners
Draft partnership agreement with capital, profit-sharing and governance provisions
Declaration of non-bankruptcy of the General Partner
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or preliminary screening flags incomplete clauses, amend the agreement and re-execute before the same notary; corrections made within five working days do not trigger additional registry penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File registration with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing portal (lbr.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership agreement and the RCS registration form (Formulaire C) electronically; pay the statutory filing levy; upon verification of completeness and legality, the RCS assigns a registration number and triggers the official publication process.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and signatures of the General Partner and appointed manager
Proof of appointment and acceptance of the registered office
Declaration of no prior disqualification or bankruptcy of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (e.g., missing signature certification or incomplete annexes), resubmit the corrected deed through the LBR portal and address the specific query within two business days; the filing fee is not forfeited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Effect legal publication in the electronic gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the RCS automatically forwards the incorporation particulars for publication in RESA; verify the publication notice and retain the RESA PDF as legal evidence for third parties, banks and counterparties.
required_dossiers: Legal publication notice text (auto-generated by the RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains material errors, notify the LBR within five days and request a corrective publication (rectificatif) at no additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with social security, tax and beneficial ownership authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the economic activity declaration with the CCSS for employer registration; apply for a VAT number via the AEDTV using form 010 if the SCSp performs taxable transactions in Luxembourg; file the beneficial ownership declaration with the RBE within 30 days of registration identifying the General Partner and all Special Limited Partners with their exact percentage interests.
required_dossiers: General Partner identification and power of attorney
Schedule of ultimate beneficial owners and ownership percentages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE queries incomplete ownership information, file an amending declaration within 15 days; voluntary correction before the expiry of the legal deadline avoids administrative fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the business establishment permit and municipal premises clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie through the Guichet.lu single permit portal; competent commune (Commune de Luxembourg) for commercial premises approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011 for the commercial activity of revenue-based financing and royalty fund management; submit identity, good repute and qualification evidence for the General Partner or appointed manager; obtain municipal occupancy clearance and fire-safety sign-off for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Identity document and criminal record extract of the General Partner/manager
Evidence of professional qualifications or university degree for the regulated business activity
Municipal building occupancy certificate and fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests additional documentation on repute or qualifications, respond within the 15-day cure period; a refusal may be appealed before the Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie et de l'accès aux professions; municipal authority (Commune de Luxembourg).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for the commercial activity of royalty and revenue-based financing; no CSSF financial-sector license is required for non-deposit-taking, non-regulated fund activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D – Registration only (no full EIA Report required for office-based financial services with no industrial plant).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limited to municipal sewer standards per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 November 2010; zero VOC emissions (no industrial solvents); waste segregation and disposal per the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; office e-waste must be transferred to an authorized collector; energy performance certificate required for the rented office under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 November 2007.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and the Commune; structural load inspection and electrical installation conformity report; workplace occupational safety clearance per the Law of 17 June 1994 on safety and health at work; first-aid, emergency signage and evacuation drill obligations for the employed workforce.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified e-filing portal: MyGuichet.lu; official sites: acd.gouvernement.lu and aed.public.lu; business registry filings: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp: (1) execute notarized partnership deed; (2) register with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through lbr.lu to obtain the 15-digit business registration number (matricule), which is the universal tax identification number; (3) file VAT registration via Form 640 with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits) immediately if any taxable supply or intra-Community acquisition is made; (4) the ACD assigns a direct-tax identification number for the SCSp partnership return (Form 200) and partner allocation schedule; (5) non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment require no separate Luxembourg TIN unless claiming withholding-tax relief, VAT refund, or an advance pricing agreement ruling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Article 6bis LIR (income tax law) prescribes fiscal transparency for SCSp: each partner is taxed directly on allocable income. The general partner may jointly elect semi-transparent entity-level taxation (SCSp treated as Luxembourg corporate resident for CIT/NWTR) by irrevocable declaration filed with ACD with the first tax return, binding on all partners. US investors may file federal check-the-box (Form 8832) to align with transparent treatment; EU ATAD 2 implementation (law of 21 December 2018) applies hybrid mismatch disallowance rules automatically to net any deduction/non-inclusion outcomes. Advance tax rulings on financing classification are obtainable via the ACD ruling committee.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for the small-enterprise exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); however, the threshold is unavailable to non-resident entities - foreign suppliers of taxable B2B services or distance goods into Luxembourg must register without threshold before supply; registration is also mandatory for intra-Community acquisitions by a Luxembourg-established business with no de minimis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping and no continuous transaction controls (unlike Italy or Spain); no API tax-stamping regime applies. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing for suppliers to the Luxembourg public administration is operational via the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard. B2B e-invoicing remains optional; any e-invoice must ensure authenticity of origin and integrity under the VAT Law. Recurring tax-file obligations include SAF-T (Fichier d'échange standard) and EC Sales Lists (VIES/Form 53); Intrastat applies separately to goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% (zero-rating) on exports outside the EU under Article 43 VAT Law, with proof of physical removal shown within 90 days. Services: B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 20 et seq. VAT Law; Art. 44 VAT Directive) locates revenue-based financing, royalty-financing and fund management at the business customer's establishment; when the borrowing digital-brand or fund is a non-EU taxable person, the supply is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (effective 0%). Where the EU customer is taxable, reverse charge applies; supplies to EU non-taxable persons are exempt financial services (no credit). Input VAT recovery follows standard pro-rata and attribution rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) filed via the Export Control System (ECS)
Bill of Lading / CMR waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate / MT103 SWIFT payment proof recording the export consideration
Commercial invoice and underlying revenue-based financing or royalty agreement
Certificate of consignee (ECS exit certificate or third-country customs entry/warehouse proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may invalidate export zero-rating, reapply 17% VAT retroactively plus statutory arrears interest (currently 0.8% per month) for up to 5 years (10 years in fraud); monetary penalties range from 10% to 100% of the evaded VAT, and criminal prosecution carries imprisonment of up to 5 years for false export documentation (Articles 81-96 VAT Law). ACD may reopen income assessments under the same 5/10-year statutes with 50% negligence or 100% bad-faith penalties; customs surveillance runs 3 years from goods release. Clawback of previously refunded input VAT is automatic upon reversal of the zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the euro as legal tender with full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account transactions under the EU Treaty and Directive 88/361/EEC. There are no exchange control approvals, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on dividend, royalty, or profit distributions to non-resident partners or beneficiaries. The SCSp, as a fiscally transparent partnership, remits profits directly to partners, and such remittances are free of FX licensing or central bank authorization. The only compliance layer is the BCL's statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations for cross-border flows, which are informational and not restrictive. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate tax withholding at source only where Luxembourg has not granted treaty relief, and not to FX or capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation quota, or surrender obligation on export proceeds, service fees, royalty collections, or financing revenues. All EUR and foreign-currency receipts may be retained, reinvested, or disbursed freely. Cross-border payments above thresholds must be reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics (BPM6/EU methodology), but this reporting is non-punitive and carries no conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — constrained. Non-EEA digital EMIs cannot operate in Luxembourg on a standalone basis without a CSSF-issued Electronic Money Institution licence (Loi du 1er août 2018 transposing EMI Directive 2009/110/EC) or use of an authorized agent/banking partner under the passport regime. EEA-licensed EMIs may passport into Luxembourg, but the SCSp must still satisfy the EMI's own AML/KYC programme, which frequently applies stricter UBO transparency standards to pass-through partnerships. Fintech EMIs are viable for low-value receivables collection (Direct Debit ACH) but cannot serve as primary escrow or treasury rails for capital injection, given their capital-assurance and safeguarding limits; Tier-1 licensed credit institutions remain mandatory for escrowed capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule mandates physical presence of directors in Luxembourg; the AML legal framework (Loi du 12 novembre 2004 as amended, implementing AML Directives) permits remote onboarding using eIDAS-compliant electronic identification or video-identification procedures provided the bank applies equivalent assurance levels. In practice, most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one physical or live-video interview with the SCSp's general partner (GP) and any senior manager, and they additionally require verified identification of every limited partner (LP) holding a direct or indirect interest above the bank's internal threshold (often 10–25%). Remote opening is therefore legally possible but commercially difficult for a fully virtual SCSp; a local Luxembourg-resident GP or an in-person meeting with the bank's compliance officer materially accelerates onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership with undisclosed or indirect ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), especially where LPs are offshore vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO cascade chart mapped to each partner's place of establishment; notarized partnership agreement and LP subscription documents; certified register of partners (even if non-public under Luxembourg law, it must be disclosed to the bank); KYC/AML identification package for every UBO above 10%; tax-residency certificates (form 6166-equivalent / Luxembourg certificate de résidence fiscale); FATCA/CRS registration confirmation of the SCSp in the Luxembourg tax authorities' system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-based financing royalty receivables present ambiguous 'source of funds' and forward-cash-flow complexity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or internally certified financial statements; executed revenue-financing agreements and royalty-assignment deeds; invoice-level aging and collections reports for the underlying digital-brand obligors; bank statements of the funding originator evidencing clean provenance; written economic rationale and business-plan memo; ongoing monitoring file demonstrating that SME revenues flow through trackable, regulated payment channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency / shell-risk flags arising from a Special LP with minimal headcount and no distinctive business footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg substance dossier: registered office in Luxembourg; local general partner (a Luxembourg corporate GP with no automatic pass-through exemption); board and partner-meeting minutes reflecting decision-making in Luxembourg; local administration agreements with a recognised Luxembourg fiduciary/domiciliation agent; payroll/ administrative outsourcing contracts; evidence that investment management, financing decisions, and treasury functions are genuinely directed from Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment routing mismatch between inbound financing proceeds and outbound royalty/interest disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented contractual flow: LP capital injection → SCSp → brand financing disbursements → merchant revenue waterfall → royalty repayment to SCSp → distribution to LPs; complete transaction-chain diagrams; vendor and debtor due-diligence register; full travel-rule-compliant beneficiary/PONs data under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113; periodic reconciliation showing economic alignment between financing tickets and royalty streams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic exposure of non-resident LPs or obligors in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/Luxembourg sanctions compliance policy; real-time screening certificates against EU/UN/OFAC lists; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files for affected partners; clarification of any sanctioned nexus and remediation evidence; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire for jurisdictions flagged by FATF; internal waiver rationale approved by the bank's AML/CTF officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident LP capital injections into the SCSp trust account are routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank inter-entity transfers) in EUR through TARGET2, or in major convertible currencies via correspondent clearing (CHIPS/Fedwire). The remittance must carry an accurate ISO 20022 purpose code classified under BCL balance-of-payments statistics as 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (category DI.1 under BPM6 reporting), with the SCSp's name, registered office, and partnership agreement reference in the free-text field. Banks require pre-delivery of the capital-call notice, the executed partnership subscription agreement, and CSSF/AML clearance before the first credit is accepted. Any conversion of USD/GBP to EUR must be executed with the receiving Luxembourg bank under a clean FX forward or spot contract to avoid mixing of investor funds and to preserve the escrow's audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements and revenue-based financing payouts are cleared predominantly via SWIFT MT103 in EUR/USD/GBP for out-of-SEPA beneficiaries, and via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) Instant Payments or SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) within the EEA for digital-brand settlements. For structured financing tranches, banks accept Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit) rails only where a confirmed bank is the issuing counterparty and the SCSp is the beneficiary; more commonly, the SCSp disburses against investment instructions using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Other Investment – Loans' and supporting financing-agreement references. All outbound payment instructions to third-party merchant obligors or royalty originators must be pre-registered in the bank's whitelist to survive transaction-monitoring controls, and the SCSp must maintain a full payee-KYC register consistent with Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 travel-rule data transmission.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with EU-authorised credit institutions
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) executed under ISDA 2002 and subject to EMIR collateral and margin rules
FX options (European-style) for hedging known future revenue-based financing redemption cash flows
Same-day and tom-next FX swaps for settlement-liquidity conversion of royalty collections
Futures and exchange-traded FX contracts where the SCSp is a professional client and the execution venue is an EU-regulated market or MTF
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for exotic non-convertible currencies not relevant to EUR/USD or EUR/GBP exposures, and only where the counterparty is a licensed EU bank under EMIR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration or of the last annual confirmation; any change in beneficial ownership must also be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 125–5,000 and/or imprisonment up to one year under the Law of 13 January 2019; persistent default may lead the RBE/RCS to initiate court-ordered administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) of the RCS-registered SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year accounts); language of filing: Luxembourgish or French
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500–15,000 under the Law of 19 December 2002; RCS formal notice, followed by District Court proceedings for dissolution and strike-off in case of repeated failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax-transparent partnership income tax declaration (allocation of profits/losses to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year, or the extended deadline indicated in the eCDF filing portal of the ACD (calendar-year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.8% per month; administrative penalty up to 10% of the assessed tax; increased assessments and criminal fines for wilful non-declaration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg VAT return (déclaration annuelle TVA, Model 400) if the SCSp is VAT-registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April of the following calendar year; not required when the SCSp files monthly or quarterly VAT returns for the whole year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to 10% of VAT due and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; in serious cases, suspension or loss of VAT registration status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit when the SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds of the Law of 19 December 2002: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average headcount > 50; audit is also required regardless of size for regulated fund/PFS and public-interest entities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 (as amended); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted as alternative accounting framework for eligible SCSp accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must submit the RBE annual confirmation within 15 days of the anniversary of the initial registration or last confirmation; any transfer of partnership interests that changes beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days; the RBE confirmation must attest the unchanged ownership chain and updated identification data of each beneficial owner
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (members register of the SCSp)
Register of General Partner and Managers (directors register)
Minute Book (partner meetings and unanimous written resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,700–7,600 per year (EUR 2,500–7,000) for registered office, corporate agent, RBE/RCS compliance and register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500–16,000 per year (EUR 6,000–15,000) for a small-to-mid-size SCSp in revenue-based financing, depending on transaction count and consolidation needs

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined CIT plus solidarity surcharge plus municipal business tax for a Luxembourg City corporate investor; 0% at SCSp entity level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp itself pays no meaningful direct income tax; eligible royalty/financing income may benefit from the Luxembourg IP box regime (80% exemption, effective 5% CIT for qualifying IP-derived income); corporate partners may claim the participation exemption for dividends/realized capital gains, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity, and the R&D tax credit; wholly tax-transparent pass-through treatment defers taxation to each partner's residence jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No separate Luxembourg CIT return is required for the SCSp itself because the SCSp is treated as a transparent partnership. Luxembourg resident corporate or individual partners report their pro-rata shares on Form 170 (corporate income tax and municipal business tax) or Form 100 (individual income tax), respectively, filed through MyGuichet / the ACD electronic filing platform. The SCSp must nevertheless file annual accounts with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the eJustice/MyGuichet portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 30 June following the end of the fiscal year for electronic corporate and individual partner returns; annual financial statements must be filed with the RCS within 7 months of the balance sheet date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the SCSp, RCS registration number, fiscal identification number, place of effective management, legal form code for SCSp, address of the registered office, and the profit-sharing percentages of the general partner and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with no Luxembourg permanent establishment must not be included in the Luxembourg taxable basis; the return should clearly identify them as non-resident and attach a certificate of residence and, if a DTA is claimed, a Tax Residence Certificate (Formulaire 51).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from the non-dilutive revenue-based financing business: royalty-type payments, financing fees, interest-like income, deferred payment surcharges, and monetized receivables; each stream is classified as royalty, interest, or commercial business income according to the contractual terms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner has no Luxembourg PE, Luxembourg-source revenue is not reported by the partner in Luxembourg; if the partner acts through a Luxembourg GP or fixed base, a Luxembourg return must be filed for the attributable income, with an explanatory profit allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 (Deductions, adjustments, and loss carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, amortization of intangible assets, arm's-length interest expense, service fees, ATAD interest limitation computations, IP box deduction, transfer pricing adjustments, participation exemption claims, and the 17-year loss carryforward schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must substantiate beneficial ownership of royalty/financing assets and attach a country-by-country and intercompany transaction schedule if related-party transactions exceed the factual audit threshold; no loss carryforward is available to partners who have never been taxable in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on assessed corporate income tax, monthly late-payment interest of 0.7%, and administrative fines in the range of EUR 25 to EUR 5,000 depending on the size of the taxpayer; failure to file accounts with the RCS can attract penalties of up to EUR 2,000 plus publication costs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions made by an SCSp to its partners, because SCSp distributions are not statutory dividends; Luxembourg domestic dividend withholding tax is 15% only where a resident corporate or partnership vehicle is tax-opaque and distributes dividends; under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and most DTA treaties the rate is reduced to 0% for qualifying holding structures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner seeking treaty or EU Directive relief must: (i) obtain a Luxembourg Tax Residence Certificate (Formulaire 51) from the Luxembourg direct tax administration; (ii) complete the relevant DTA/refund application identifying the beneficial owner, article, and amount of income; (iii) attach a signed partnership deed, audited financial statements, and proof of economic substance in Luxembourg; (iv) submit the package to the ACD within the statutory filing window; where a withholding was already borne, a refund claim must be filed within 5 years of the end of the calendar year of withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outgoing interest or royalty payments; correspondingly, DTA rates are often 0% for pure interest and royalty payments under the Luxembourg treaties with France, Germany, the Netherlands, and the United States, and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive eliminates withholding on qualifying EU related-party payments if the recipient holds at least 25% of the Luxembourg payer, or both are held by a 25% EU parent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg law does not codify a specific local file/master file threshold, but the tax administration expects contemporaneous transfer pricing study documentation for all material related-party cross-border financing and royalty transactions, typically as from EUR 250,000 in annual transaction value; CbC notification and master file obligations arise for large groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no license-based Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the type used in certain Gulf jurisdictions, but substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit), the ATAD interest stripping limitation, and the requirement that the SCSp has a genuine Luxembourg office, local professional advisors, Luxembourg bank accounts, real decision-making records, and a locally resident general partner; a letterbox SCSp with no substantive management may be disregarded and its income reattributed to the controlling partners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Wilful Concealment of Taxable Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare revenue-based financing income, deliberately treating finance fees as tax-exempt capital distributions, backdating the partnership deed, or allocating profits to a zero-tax partner with no economic entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties under Luxembourg law: imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to EUR 100,000 per assessment; civil tax reassessment plus late-payment interest of 0.7% per month and a late-filing or understatement surcharge of 10% of the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate general partner and its directors are jointly and severally liable for the underpaid corporate tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; criminal courts may additionally order director disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment for intentional concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an SCSp with no physical presence, no Luxembourg-based general partner, no board minutes, no local bank account, and using the entity solely to redeploy royalty income to a tax-favored non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may disregard the partnership under Article 56bis LIR, reallocate the royalty/financing income to the principal taxpayers, deny treaty benefits, and impose penalties on unreported income; the commercial register may also de-register the company (rayure d'office) for persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally liable for resultant tax assessments if they implemented or knowingly benefited from the artificial structure; criminal sanctions for organizers of artificial tax arrangements include imprisonment, restitution orders, and international travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the royalty financing fund without appointing a Luxembourg AML compliance officer, failing to verify ultimate beneficial owners of the digital-brand debtors, accepting payments from shell debtors, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering, administrative fines of up to EUR 5 million for legal persons and EUR 2 million for individuals; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for aggravated money laundering; CSSF or the AML supervisor may impose supervisory fines and freeze fund assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and its board of directors may be prosecuted criminally; personal liability extends to civil restitution of laundered amounts, travel bans pending investigation, and imprisonment for intentional non-compliance with AML obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Aggressive Royalty Financing Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the royalty base, financing spread, or guarantee fee above or below the arm's length range solely to shift profits to a zero-tax partner; executing circular loan/licence structures with no genuine economic flows or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment recharacterizing the transaction at arm's length, interest charge on underpaid tax at 0.7% per month, penalties for understatement of tax reaching 30% to 50% of the additional tax, and mandatory publication of the tax adjustment in certain cases of aggressive tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign the manipulated transfer pricing documentation may be jointly and severally liable for the additional tax; in cases of fraudulent TP documentation, personal criminal liability includes fines, confiscation orders, and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
